speaker: Doctor
text: Does the child have a history of excessive bleeding from minor cuts, prolonged bleeding after vaccinations, or any episodes of blood in his urine or stool?

text: My main symptom is Swelling of the right knee. I also have No recent trauma or injury, Familial history of similar symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: The prolonged aPTT with a normal PT suggests a deficiency in the intrinsic pathway, such as Hemophilia A or B. REQUEST TEST: Factor_VIII_Level

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the coagulation factors are normal, I need to rule out other causes of hemarthrosis. Do you have a family history of von Willebrand disease, or does the child have a history of easy bruising? REQUEST TEST: Von_Willebrand_Factor_Assay

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal coagulation profile and family history, I suspect a hereditary arthropathy like juvenile idiopathic arthritis or a dysplasia. REQUEST TEST: Knee_MRI

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal MRI rules out structural or inflammatory causes, so I need to reconsider the bleeding tendency. Does the child have a history of bleeding after circumcision or dental procedures, and is the family history specifically on the maternal side? REQUEST TEST: Factor_XI_Level

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal coagulation factors and MRI, I suspect a non-clotting disorder like synovial chondromatosis or a metabolic issue. REQUEST TEST: Joint_Fluid_Analysis

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ultrasound Knee Findings: Compatible with hemarthrosis of the right knee, no evidence of fracture or dislocation.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound confirms hemarthrosis despite normal standard coagulation factors, which in a male child with a maternal family history strongly points to a sex-linked recessive bleeding disorder like Hemophilia A or B, potentially missed by initial screening or representing a variant. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia
